text:
[LTIM.2.8.2] **The monotonic clock** never decreases. Its zero is
unspecified: only the difference between two of its readings has a meaning, and
the runtime **must not** give a single reading any other (process uptime, time
since engine creation, a calendar instant).

Its range is the `Duration` range ([LTIM.1.3.1]): 0 to $2^{63} - 1$
nanoseconds. A host call that would move it past the top returns
`DS_ERR_TIME_RANGE` ([NTST.3.1], [LTIM.1.1.5]). The runtime **must** hold a
live reading past the top at the top ([NLFC.5.4]), so the clock neither wraps
nor decreases.

Every relative-time mechanism **must** read the monotonic clock and no other:
TTL expiry, `after`, a call's `timeout`, `cooldown`, a single pattern's `within`,
`dwell` and series windows. A change to the wall clock therefore moves none of them.

A sequence's `within` (`then … within`) is not one of them. It bounds when the
events **happened**, not when the engine received them, so it compares the
facts' own `ts` values ([LTHE.2.2.2]), which are event time.

idris.name: lcdb_3_2_1_1__rhs_gated
idris.note: `cooldown` reads the monotonic clock and no other: the gate's instant is the net's clock, the monotonic sample, and the wall clock is nowhere in this engine.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__mono_test_of
idris.note: THE MONOTONIC TIMED TEST OF A `where`: the test read at the monotonic sample with the wall fixed at zero. What the runner builds for a `where` with no `now()`, so that it is a monotonic gate of Rete/NetworkTwoClocks.idr by construction.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__mono_test_of_agrees
idris.note: AND IT IS THE TIMED TEST, PAIR BY PAIR, for a `where` with no `now()`: at every sample, token and candidate the two answer alike, since a leaf that reads no wall sample is substituted alike at any wall. Stated pointwise, since two join functions that agree on every pair are not identified without extensionality, which is why the runner builds the monotonic form rather than deriving it.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__mono_test_of_monotonic
idris.note: THE MONOTONIC TIMED TEST IS A MONOTONIC GATE: at one monotonic sample it is one function of the pair, whatever the wall. A TRANSCRIPTION by construction on the monotonic component, as Rete/NetworkTwoClocks.idr's `ltim_2_7_1__within_gate_monotonic` is; it fails if the test is changed to read the wall and refutes nothing else. What lets C2 (`ltim_2_8_2__pump_ignores_wall`) instantiate on a lowered `where`.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__read_ignores_wall
idris.note: A LEAF THAT READS NO WALL SAMPLE IS SUBSTITUTED ALIKE AT TWO WALL SAMPLES: `monotonic_ns()` and `dwell` read the monotonic component and the stamps, nothing of the wall, over every pair of wall samples, stamp table and token.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__reads_wall
idris.note: WHETHER A `where` READS THE WALL CLOCK: a `now()` leaf anywhere in it. `dwell` and `within`, as lowered, read the monotonic clock and no other: the criterion answers `False` on `ReadMono` and `ReadDwell`.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__subst_ignores_wall
idris.note: AND SO IS A `where` WITH NO `now()`: substituted at `(m, w)` and at `(m, w')` it is one expression, over every expression, stamp table and token. By induction on the expression. 'A change to the wall clock therefore moves none of them', for `dwell` and `within` as lowered.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__due_stamped_monotonic
idris.note: THE GATE FORM IS A MONOTONIC GATE at every stamp table: it reads the monotonic sample and the stamps, nothing of the wall. C2's hypothesis, inhabited; a TRANSCRIPTION of Rete/NetworkTwoClocks.idr's `dwell_gate_monotonic`, said so.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__guard
idris.note: A `where` with no `now()`, built in the monotonic form: a monotonic gate by construction. A fixture.

idris.name: Ltim_2_8_2__monotonic
idris.note: A MONOTONIC GATE: a two-clock test that answers at `(m, w)` what it answers at `(m, w')`. A gate on elapsed monotonic time, the clause's 'reads the monotonic clock and no other'.

idris.name: Ltim_2_8_2__monotonic_all
idris.note: Every test monotonic, chain by chain.

idris.name: iret_19_5__retime_clocked_wall
idris.note: The re-time stage at two wall samples: one state.

idris.name: iret_19_5__tick_chain_wall
idris.note: One chain re-timed under a monotonic gate at two wall samples: one chain.

idris.name: iret_19_5__tick_chains_wall
idris.note: And every chain.

idris.name: iret_19_5__tick_clocked_wall
idris.note: The composed tick at two wall samples: one state. The sweep reads no test; the re-time stage is the lemma above.

idris.name: lexp_9_5_1__dwell_fires_once_executed
idris.note: C3a EXECUTED: the one-fact program under `dwell >= 2` from a stamp of 0, over ticks 1, 2, 3, 4, fires once, at 2, and never again: `[0, 1, 0, 0]`, total 1.

idris.name: lexp_9_5_1__dwell_gate_monotonic
idris.note: And so is `dwell`. A TRANSCRIPTION on the same terms.

idris.name: lexp_9_5_1__dwell_ignores_wall_executed
idris.note: C2 EXECUTED: over the samples of `wall_gate_reopens`, whose wall goes 1, 2, 1, 2, the `dwell >= 2` gate fires once, at the monotonic sample 2, `[0, 1, 0, 0]`; over the same monotonic samples with every wall sample rewritten to 9, the same.

idris.name: lexp_9_5_1__dwell_tests_monotonic
idris.note: C2'S HYPOTHESIS, INHABITED: the one `dwell` test is monotonic at every stamp table.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__rising_edges_at_most_one
idris.note: C3a. A RISING GATE'S EDGES OVER ANY TICK HISTORY SUM TO AT MOST ONE: it rises once or not at all, because the composed engine's clock never goes back. 'A gate that stays true once true fires once per wrapper', as a count.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__rising_fires_at_most_once
idris.note: C3a ON THE ENGINE, with part B: the one-fact program under a rising gate fires AT MOST ONCE over any tick history from any starting clock. Once per false-to-true edge, and a rising gate has at most one. The hypothesis is inhabited by `lexp_9_5_1__dwell_gate_rising` and executed by `lexp_9_5_1__dwell_fires_once_executed`.

idris.name: ltim_2_7_1__within_gate_monotonic
idris.note: `within` is a monotonic gate: it reads the monotonic sample alone, so at one monotonic sample it is one function of the pair, whatever the wall. A TRANSCRIPTION, `Refl` by construction on the monotonic component; it fails if the gate is changed to read the wall and refutes nothing else.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__counts_ignore_wall
idris.note: C2 OVER A HISTORY: with every test monotonic at every stamp table, the counts of a sample history are unmoved by any rewriting of its wall samples. The wall clock may be set anywhere, at any step, and `dwell`, `within` and every other gate on elapsed monotonic time fire as they would have.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__pump_ignores_wall
idris.note: C2. THE WALL CLOCK MOVES NO FIRING OF A MONOTONIC GATE: when every test is a gate on elapsed monotonic time, the pump at `(m, w)` and the pump at `(m, w')` leave one engine, with one halt and one count. `dwell` and `within` on the composed engine are moved by no wall clock, as the clause requires of every relative-time mechanism. The hypothesis is inhabited by `lexp_9_5_1__dwell_tests_monotonic` and executed by `lexp_9_5_1__dwell_ignores_wall_executed`.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__held
idris.note: `dwell >= 3`: logical/LTIM.2.8.2_wall_step_moves_no_dwell's `held`. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__one_mono_rule
idris.note: ONE RULE IN THE RUNNER'S MONOTONIC FORM over kind 0, action-free, its node loaded with the monotonic test at the sample (0, 0): what `Fixture.idr` builds for a `where` with no `now()`. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__one_mono_test_monotonic
idris.note: THE RUNNER'S MONOTONIC TEST INHABITS C2'S HYPOTHESIS: the one-rule test list of a `where` with no `now()`, built in Rete/NetworkTimed.idr's monotonic form, is monotonic at every stamp table, for every environment and expression. What lets the theorem below be read on every lowered `dwell` and `within`.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__one_mono_tests
idris.note: The one monotonic rule's tests, by ordinal. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__wall_step_moves_no_monotonic_pump
idris.note: C2 ON THIS ENGINE. A WALL STEP MOVES NO FIRING OF A MONOTONIC `where`: with every timed test a monotonic gate over the state's stamps, the pump after a wall step to any instant and the pump without it leave one gated state -- the net, the clock, the deadlines, the rows, the trackers -- one halt and one trace; the wall sample alone differs. Over every program, cooldown list, test list, fuel, net, pair of wall samples, stamp table and tracker table. The entry re-time at the two wall samples is one net (Rete/NetworkTwoClocks.idr's `iret_19_5__retime_clocked_wall`), and the run from it projects to Rete/NetworkCooldown.idr's gated run from the projected state, which carries no wall (Rete/NetworkTimed.idr's `ltim_2_4_2__run_timed_projects`). 'A change to the wall clock therefore moves none of them', for `dwell` and `within` as the Idris model lowers them, on the engine the Idris model runs. The hypothesis is inhabited by `ltim_2_8_2__one_mono_test_monotonic` and executed by `ltim_2_8_2__wall_steps_move_no_dwell_timed`.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__wall_steps_move_no_dwell_timed
idris.note: WALL STEPS MOVE NO `dwell`: the wall set to 10 before the Ping; an advance to 5 and a pump fire `held`; the wall stepped back to 9 and a pump, forward to 16 and a pump, an advance to 6 and a pump fire nothing -- logical/LTIM.2.8.2_wall_step_moves_no_dwell's shape, C2 executed on the Idris model's engine. Executed: `[[(0, True)], [], [], []]`.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__now_test_is_not_monotonic
idris.note: 'Every relative-time mechanism must read the monotonic clock and no other': `now()` is not one of them, and its test is not a monotonic gate, by refutation.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__cooled
idris.note: A cooldown has run: at least `window` since the last firing, on the monotonic clock. Reduced to its clock dependence; the gate itself is Rete/RateGate.idr's.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__cooled_ignores_wall
idris.note: NOR ANY COOLDOWN. A TRANSCRIPTION: the mechanism is defined on the monotonic component, so this is `Refl`; it fails if the definition is changed to read the wall clock and refutes nothing else.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__cooled_ignores_zero
idris.note: Nor does any cooldown.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__difference_ignores_zero
idris.note: Moving the zero: a difference of two readings taken `k` later on the dial is the difference it was. By induction on the shift.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__dwell_ignores_wall
idris.note: A WALL CLOCK SET ANYWHERE MOVES NO `dwell`. A TRANSCRIPTION: the mechanism is defined on the monotonic component, so this is `Refl`; it fails if the definition is changed to read the wall clock and refutes nothing else.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__dwell_ignores_zero
idris.note: THE ZERO IS UNSPECIFIED, AND NO `dwell` DEPENDS ON IT: a monotonic clock that counts from `k` later gives every fact the `dwell` it had. 'Only the difference between two of its readings has a meaning.'

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__in_window
idris.note: A series window's membership: a value absorbed at a monotonic sample is in a window of `w` while it entered less than `w` ago -- `within`'s formula on the sample at which it was absorbed. A stand-in for the mechanism, reduced to its clock dependence: which members a query's discount admits after an eviction ([LSIG.2.5.1]) is SeriesWindow.idr's, and the discounted value is not modelled.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__in_window_ignores_wall
idris.note: NOR A SERIES WINDOW'S MEMBERSHIP. A TRANSCRIPTION: the mechanism is defined on the monotonic component, so this is `Refl`; it fails if the definition is changed to read the wall clock and refutes nothing else.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__in_window_ignores_zero
idris.note: Nor does a series window's membership, which is `within`'s.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__order_ignores_zero
idris.note: And an order of two readings is the order it was. By induction on the shift.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__reached
idris.note: A deadline on the monotonic clock is reached -- a TTL's expiry, an `after` timer's `fire_at`. Inclusive, as for expiry ([RARC.5.2.4]). Reduced to its clock dependence; the sweep itself is Rete/TtlSweep.idr's.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__reached_ignores_wall
idris.note: NOR ANY DEADLINE: no TTL expires and no timer comes due because the host clock was set. A TRANSCRIPTION: the mechanism is defined on the monotonic component, so this is `Refl`; it fails if the definition is changed to read the wall clock and refutes nothing else.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__reached_ignores_zero
idris.note: Nor does any deadline: a shift of the zero is carried through the comparison.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__within_ignores_wall
idris.note: NOR ANY `within`. A TRANSCRIPTION: the mechanism is defined on the monotonic component, so this is `Refl`; it fails if the definition is changed to read the wall clock and refutes nothing else.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__within_ignores_zero
idris.note: Nor does any `within`: a shift of the zero is carried through the subtraction.
